newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern bids for Conrail.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern bids for Conrail.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp, as expected, topped rival CSX Corp's bid for Conrail Inc with an all-cash offer of $100 per share.
CSX has bid $92.50 per share for Conrail in cash and stock.
Norfolk Southern said it has commitments for $4 billion of the necessary financing for its bid from Merrill Lynch and J.P. Morgan.
Norfolk said its tender is for all outstanding common shares and Series A ESOP convertible junior preferred shares.

"This proposal is better on every point than the CSX/Conrail proposal announced last week," Norfolk Southern Chairman David Goode said in a press release. "A combined Norfolk Southern-Conrail will create a more balanced eastern rail system and will do so by increasing rather than diminishing competition in the industry."
Norfolk said its bid represents a premium of $11.49 per share, or 13 percent, over the blended value of CSX's 40 percent cash and 60 percent stock proposal.

Norfolk Southern said its offer will be accomplished by a cash tender for all outstanding shares of Conrail, followed by a merger in which Conrail's remaining shareholders would receive the same cash purchase price.
The deal will provide for a voting trust to hold the Conrail shares acquired in the tender, allowing shareholders to receive immediate payment for their stock.
The tender offer is conditioned on an opinion from the Surface Transportation Board that the use of the voting trust is consistent with policies of the board.
The deal is also subject to financing, the valid tender of a majority of Conrail shares, redemption of Conrail's poison pill, and termination of the CSX offer.
Norfolk said it has a letter from Merrill Lynch and J.P. Morgan indicating they are highly confident that the balance of financing needed is available.
Norfolk previously objected to the proposed $8.4 billion CSX-Conrail merger.
In a letter to Conrail Chairman David LeVan, Goode said he had attempted in September and early October to discuss acquiring Conrail.
CSX announced its deal with Conrail on October 15.
Norfolk said it was willing to meet with Conrail. It also said it had started litigation in federal court in Pennsylvania against Conrail.

In the letter, Goode said Norfolk would consider moving its headquarters to Philadelphia, where Conrail is based, and would be willing to discuss opportunities for Conrail senior management, as well as significnant representation on the Norfolk board for Conrail directors.
Goode's letter was made public by Norfolk.
